newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's NSGB net profit up 17.8 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's NSGB net profit up 17.8 pct in 1996.

text.p: French-dominated National Societe Generale Bank made net after-tax profits of 56.984 million pounds ($16.78 million) in calendar 1996, 17.8 percent up on 48.393 million in 1995, the bank said on Wednesday.
The profits are equivalent to 56.98 pounds for each of the one million shares, which closed on Tuesday at 1,015 pounds on the Egyptian stock exchange.

The bank's total balance sheet rose to 3.198 billion pounds at the end of 1996 from 3.005 billion a year earlier, the bank said in a published announcement. Total revenue increased to 298.168 million pounds from 256.360 million.
At the end of the year the bank's provisions stood at 142.504 million pounds, from 115.814 a year earlier.
At its ordinary meeting on March 19, the general assembly agreed to increase the bank's capital to 120 million pounds from 100 million by issuing one free share for each five.
It also approved a proposal to distribute a cash dividend of 20 pounds per share.
National Societe Generale is 51 percent owned by Societe Generale of France.
State-owned National Bank of Egypt, which was once the majority shareholder, holds now 18 percent and the rest of the shares are traded on the stock exchange.
